title: Lattice Filter - GPS L1 (1575 MHz) for 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Stefan Richter

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Lattice Filter filter targeting GPS L1 (1575 MHz) for 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module. The filter is designed on Quartz substrate with a target center frequency of 1352.1 MHz and bandwidth of 73.1 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Lattice Filter
- Frequency Band: GPS L1 (1575 MHz)
- Application: 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module
- Substrate: Quartz
- Package: LGA (Land Grid Array)
- Design Tool: Cadence AWR Microwave Office
- Design Center: Andover HQ Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Lattice Filter design targeting GPS L1 (1575 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1352.1 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       73.1 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.4 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 20.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 52.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 31.0 dB
Q Factor:               12053
Temperature Coefficient:-9.7 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.8 x 1.1 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   8
Electrode Material:     W
Passivation:            SiO2/Si3N4 stack
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Cadence AWR Microwave Office and load the Lattice Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: Quartz with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1352.1 MHz, BW 73.1 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.4 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (LGA (Land Grid Array)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, Quartz).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Anritsu MS46122B ShockLine.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 4056 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.4 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 20.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 110 MHz offset >= 52.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 10 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 1.6 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +32 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 88%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-08-09
Devices Tested:         66
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.06 dB
Return Loss (meas):     22.0 dB
Rejection (meas):       54.6 dB
Isolation (meas):       36.0 dB
Q Factor (meas):        12053
Group Delay Variation:  1.7 ns
Power Handling:         +32 dBm
Die Yield:              86.0%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Lattice Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for GPS L1 (1575 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Package parasitic effects were consistent with 3D EM model predictions.
e) ESD robustness exceeded specification by 2x margin.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
